## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Non-ASCII titles lose their accented letters or produce an empty slug, so different pages can end up with the same URL. The pull-request description also needs the `## Testing` section that project policy requires.

## Changes
The pull request adds `slugify` in `app/slug.py`, which lowercases a title, collapses each run of characters outside `[a-z0-9]` into one hyphen and trims hyphens from both ends. It also adds parametrized tests in `tests/test_slug.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/slug.py:7 — correctness — Handle non-ASCII letters in titles — `slugify("Café Menu")` returns `"caf-menu"` and `slugify("日本語")` returns `""`, because `[^a-z0-9]+` treats all non-ASCII letters as separators. The PR body promises to replace only "non-alphanumeric characters", and Python counts `é` as alphanumeric. — Pages with non-English titles get truncated slugs or empty slugs, and empty slugs make different pages share the same URL. — Fix: Either transliterate first (`unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", ...)` and drop combining marks) or match `[\W_]+` with `re.UNICODE`, then add a non-ASCII case to `test_slugify`.

- PR body — correctness — Add a `## Testing` section to the description — The description contains only one summary sentence and no `## Testing` section, which breaks AGENTS.md:4: "Every pull-request description has a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified." — Maintainers can't tell from the description how the change was verified.
